title: Parapneumonic Effusion and Empyema: Staging, Light Criteria, VATS and Decortication
subject: ss-ctvs

MIST-2 Randomized Clinical Trial (tPA and DNase in Pleural Infection)

steps.say: Evaluating an undifferentiated pleural effusion begins with thoracentesis and chemical analysis. Light criteria differentiate between transudative and exudative pleural effusions with high sensitivity. An effusion is classified as an exudate if the pleural fluid to serum protein ratio exceeds zero point five, or if the lactate dehydrogenase ratio exceeds zero point six.
steps.tx: Application of **Light criteria** provides the gold standard **exudate definition** for pleural fluid analysis. A fluid is classified as an exudate if the **protein ratio** (pleural to serum) exceeds 0.5, the **LDH ratio** exceeds 0.6, or pleural fluid LDH exceeds two-thirds the upper limit of normal serum LDH (ratio >2/3 normal).

rows: >2/3 upper limit of normal serum LDH
<=2/3 upper limit of normal serum LDH
Systemic hydrostatic pressure or low oncotic pressure

steps.say: Parapneumonic pleural effusions evolve through three distinct pathological phases over days to weeks, which is recognized by surgical teams. The exudative stage features sterile, thin, free-flowing fluid that responds to antibiotics. If untreated, bacterial invasion triggers the fibropurulent stage with heavy fibrin loculation. The organizing stage traps the lung under a dense fibroblastic cortex.
steps.tx: Parapneumonic infection evolves through 3 distinct chronological phases: **Stage 1 exudative** phase, characterized by sterile, free-flowing serous fluid; **Stage 2 fibropurulent** phase, featuring dense fibrin septation, multiloculation, and bacterial invasion; and **Stage 3 organizing** phase, where fibroblast proliferation forms an unyielding collagenous peel, producing a chronic **trapped lung**.

left.title: Stage 1 (Exudative Phase)
points: Thin, clear, sterile free-flowing pleural fluid
Tube thoracostomy rarely required unless large

right.title: Stage 2 and 3 (Fibropurulent / Organizing)
points: Bacterial invasion, dense fibrin, and loculations
Acidic pH (<7.20) and low glucose (<40-60 mg/dL)
Thick collagenous peel incarcerates lung parenchyma
Requires VATS debridement or open decortication

steps.say: A complicated parapneumonic effusion indicates active bacterial invasion into the pleural space. Bacterial metabolism consumes glucose and generates lactic acid, lowering pleural fluid pH below seven point two zero. A glucose level below forty to sixty milligrams per decilitre and LDH over one thousand units mandate chest tube insertion, which is recognized by surgical teams.
steps.tx: A **complicated parapneumonic effusion** requires mandatory tube thoracostomy drainage, defined by a **pleural fluid pH** below 7.20, **glucose** below 40 to 60 mg/dL, **LDH** greater than 1000 IU/L, or a positive Gram stain or culture. Relying on systemic antibiotics alone without tube drainage leads to loculation and sepsis.

steps.say: Overt empyema represents the macroscopic accumulation of thick pus within the pleural cavity, which is recognized by surgical teams. The fluid is thick, opaque, and foul-smelling, populated by dead neutrophils and bacteria. Empyema represents a true surgical abscess that will never resolve with antibiotics alone, requiring complete drainage.
steps.tx: Establishing an **empyema definition** requires the macroscopic identification of **frank pus** upon pleural aspiration. An established empyema functions physiologically as a closed intrathoracic abscess that will never resolve with systemic antibiotics alone, mandating immediate, complete **mechanical drainage** via large-bore chest tube or thoracoscopy.

steps.say: In patients with multiloculated empyema who fail chest tube drainage, intrapleural enzymatic therapy can clear fibrinous debris. The MIST-2 trial established that combining tissue plasminogen activator with recombinant deoxyribonuclease improves drainage. Administering tPA ten milligrams and DNase five milligrams twice daily for three days avoids surgery.
steps.tx: The landmark **MIST-2 trial** demonstrated that combined **intrapleural fibrinolysis** using **tPA and DNase** significantly enhances fluid evacuation and reduces surgical referrals. The protocol instills 10 mg of tPA and 5 mg of human recombinant DNase twice daily for 3 days, dissolving fibrin septations and cleaving free bacterial DNA.

nodes.label: CT demonstrates multiloculated Stage 2 parapneumonic effusion failing tube
Instill intrapleural tPA (10 mg) and DNase (5 mg) into chest tube
Clamp tube for 1 to 2 hours to allow enzymatic fibrin and DNA lysis
Release clamp to low negative suction; repeat twice daily for 3 days (6 doses)

steps.say: Video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery is the surgical treatment of choice for early multiloculated empyema. In stage two disease, thoracoscopy enables thorough mechanical disruption of all fibrinous loculations, which is recognized by surgical teams. The surgeon aspirates gelatinous purulent exudate, breaks down fibrous webs, and positions large chest tubes under direct vision.
steps.tx: Early **VATS debridement** represents the operative standard for **Stage 2 empyema** that fails tube thoracostomy. Under thoracoscopic visualization, the surgeon performs mechanical **loculation breakdown**, evacuates gelatinous fibrin debris, irrigates the pleural space with warm saline, and positions large-bore chest drains directly into dependent gutters.

vis.alt: Surgical pathology and thoracoscopic debridement of multiloculated empyema.

steps.say: Chronic stage three organizing empyema forms a thick fibrous peel that encases the visceral pleura and traps the lung. Once an unyielding peel develops, thoracoscopic suction is insufficient. Surgeons perform open decortication via posterolateral thoracotomy, carefully peeling the fibrous cortex off the lung to achieve full re-expansion.
steps.tx: In chronic Stage 3 disease, a thick, collagenous **fibroblastic peel** incarcerates the pulmonary parenchyma, causing restrictive atelectasis. Management requires **open decortication** via thoracotomy to meticulously dissect and strip the fibrous peel from the visceral pleura, achieving complete **pulmonary re-expansion** and obliterating the residual pleural dead space.

nodes.label: Posterolateral thoracotomy entered through 5th or 6th intercostal space
Incise thick parietal peel and enter extrapleural cleavage plane
Meticulously peel visceral fibrous cortex off entrapped pulmonary lobes
Inflate lungs under 30 cm H2O airway pressure to verify complete expansion

steps.say: Postpneumonectomy empyema with a bronchopleural fistula is one of the most formidable thoracic surgical challenges. Emergency management requires immediate chest tube drainage to prevent drowning of the remaining lung. Subsequent care requires open window thoracostomy with an Eloesser flap or Clagett procedure to sterilize the cavity.
steps.tx: The catastrophic combination of postpneumonectomy empyema and **bronchopleural fistula** requires emergent dependent pleural drainage to protect the contralateral lung from aspirated pus. Definitive control employs an open window thoracostomy, such as an **Eloesser flap** or **Clagett procedure**, followed by delayed cavity closure with antibiotic solution or muscle transposition.

rows: Immediate tube thoracostomy or dependent cannula
Prevents lethal aspiration of purulent fluid into solitary remaining lung
Provides long-term dependent open cavity drainage and daily packing
Cavity debridement and antiseptic dressing changes
Granulates pleural walls and clears bacterial colonization
Clagett procedure or intrathoracic muscle transposition
Fistula closure with latissimus/pectoralis flap and antibiotic fluid fill
